dedupe_keys.name: bipm circular t monthly utc utc k differences for about 80 timing laboratories

description: Circular T is the monthly publication of the BIPM Time Department that gives traceability to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) for the local realisations UTC(k) kept by national timing institutes. Each issue gives the differences [UTC - UTC(k)] every five days for about 80 institutes that regularly send clock and clock comparison data to the BIPM, with other information used to compute these values, such as uncertainties and the relation of UTC to International Atomic Time. The page lists issues from number 125 up to number 464 of August 2026. Coverage: about 80 national laboratories worldwide, monthly issues since the 1990s. Format and access: PDF and text files on the BIPM website and time FTP server, free. Caveats: published after the month ends, so not real time; UTC(k) of a laboratory is not the time delivered by every network or GNSS receiver in that country. Simulation uses: reference offsets of national time scales for studies of timing resilience, for example how far networks that rely on GNSS or national time servers could drift during an outage. Related records: data-nist-internet-time-service-servers and data-ntp-pool-project-servers deliver time from such laboratories and volunteers to networks; data-igs-gnss-products gives satellite clock products; data-nist-tn-2189-critical-infrastructure-gps-timing gives the GPS timing dependence of critical infrastructure.
